Is there such game, where you just play the final Dungeon, and keep getting rebirth? Like you enter the tower, get some random loots. You will be able to allocate stats, rescue random party members. Then fight the final boss.
When you get defeated, you just get reincarnated into the next "Hero" with new allies, until you official beat the game and the RNG God? Oh the boss will always get the counter skills you will get too, so you cant memorize. The build set in your previous play wont be effective in your current.
I think this would be pretty cool though.

posts.author: Gensun
posts.body:
Depending on what you mean by "five minutes" the game couldn't exist. A solid boss fight should be expected to last five minutes. If you decide to add a little bit of story, even a basic one, it can take five minutes for a player to get through the intro. If you're dealing with stat allocation expect a solid five minutes just for the player to read skill and stat descriptions.
You're probably looking for a 'roguelite' game which don't tend to last "five minutes".
I strongly suggest playing through some recent christmas jam games to see what a 20-minute game looks like, and they're much thinner in terms of available mechanics:

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
A game like this doesn't seem like it would be hard to program, but the key would be in the game play and design decisions.
Since the entire game is short and pretty much exclusively about combat, the combat system would have to be really fun. Otherwise, I think players could get bored pretty fast.
And I'm not sure I would want to invest time learning about the character/party skills and such, just to do a couple minute fight and then lose to try again.
And there would have to be some appreciable variety and differences in what you can initially chose or initially get. Otherwise it is just do the same fight over and over again.
I think a big part would be the amount of time the player needs to invest to be able to effectively fight the boss compared to how long the boss fight actually takes.
You could add something where if you defeat one boss, you move on to another one.
The question I would have in designing such a game would be what is the incentive for the player to play the game? What will be fun about it? And what is the incentive for the player to keep playing the game? To keep trying to beat the boss?
Interesting concept though.

Think of it like a card game, there are card games that are really short! or think of it like the DnD game format, except your pressured to make decisions - roll the die and drop the cards.
When you start the game, everything is already pre generated, and the player just needs to find all of them, and make the right decisions for the unknown. Just like the card game - poker, you gamble and gamble, until you win. This is how this kind of short RPG will get players interested.
I think the carryon will be the completion list - the items you collect, the skills you collect, the combinations you had will be carried on. I like this because of the anime Re-Zero.

thank you for pointing me to the genre of rogue like - i was able to come across SLAY THE SPIRE - never knowing what build you gonna end up with! this is definitely a good inspiration, also the binding of isaac - live die repeat!
But my idea for this game mechanics is from a game im actually playing for an END GAME mode. There are 30 floors, and you get 3 options each floor - fight for coins and recruit, open a chest, activate an event. a boss every 5th floor, and a specialty shop every 9th floor. All characters are max level, and optimized equip. So the challenge is getting the right characters, the team comp matters as there are super buffs as you make a certain team composition. The actual game is already hard as it is a grid battle with time reactions for skill activation. But i will try to simplify it in this 5-min game.
